column1: capture|To catch something and keep hold of it.|The game lets us capture a flag.
captures|Catches something and keeps hold of it.|The player captures a flag in our game.
captured|Caught something and kept hold of it.|Our team captured the flag in the game.
capturing|Catching something or saving it in a picture.|I am capturing the sunset with my camera.
figure|A shape or a small model of a person.|I made a small figure out of clay.
figures|Shapes or small models of people.|We made clay figures for our story.
figurine|A small model of a person or animal.|There is a tiny rabbit figurine on the shelf.
figurines|Small models of people or animals.|We made animal figurines from clay.
future|The time that has not happened yet.|In the future, I would like to be a vet.
futuristic|Looking like something from an imagined future.|My drawing shows a futuristic flying bus.
manufacture|To make things, often in a factory.|This factory will manufacture toy trains.

mixture|Two or more things mixed together.|Stir the cake mixture with a spoon.

mixers|Tools or machines for mixing things.|The bakers use large mixers for their dough.
puncture|A small hole made by something sharp.|My bicycle tyre has a puncture.

punctured|Made a small hole in something.|A thorn punctured my bicycle tyre.
puncturing|Making a small hole in something.|The thorn was puncturing the soft rubber tyre.
receipt|A note showing what you bought and paid for.|The shop gave us a receipt for the crayons.
receipts|Notes showing what you bought and paid for.|We kept the shop receipts in a little folder.
premature|Happening too soon, before something is ready.|It was premature to pack away the game before we had finished.
prematurely|Too soon, before something is ready.|We opened the oven prematurely, before the cake was ready.
vulture|A large bird that often eats animals that have died.|We saw a vulture flying high above the hills.
vultures|Large birds that often eat animals that have died.|The vultures spread their wide wings.
adventures|Exciting experiences or journeys.|We imagined adventures in a magical forest.
adventurer|Someone who goes on exciting journeys.|The young adventurer explored a hidden valley in the story.
adventurers|People who go on exciting journeys.|The adventurers followed the map to the old tower.
adventurous|Happy to try new or exciting things.|Our adventurous class tried a new outdoor game.
creatures|Animals or imaginary living things.|Tiny creatures live under the garden stones.
furnish|To put furniture in a room.|We will furnish the reading corner with comfy chairs.
furnishes|Puts furniture in a room.|The shop furnishes the room with tables and chairs.
furnished|Filled a room with furniture.|We furnished the doll's house with tiny chairs.
furnishing|Putting furniture in a room.|We are furnishing the new reading corner.
naturally|In a way that happens without people making it happen.|The seeds spread naturally in the wind.
pictures|Drawings, paintings or photographs.|We painted pictures of our favourite animals.
pictured|Shown or imagined in a picture.|The bird pictured on this page has blue wings.
picturing|Imagining how something looks.|I am picturing a castle with purple towers.
ceilings|The top inside surfaces of rooms.|The old house has high ceilings.
deceives|Makes someone believe something that is not true.|The fox deceives the other animals in the story.
deceived|Made someone believe something that was not true.|The story's fox deceived the other animals.
deceiving|Making someone believe something that is not true.|The fox was deceiving the other animals in the story.
deceit|Words or actions that make someone believe a lie.|The story teaches us that deceit can hurt our friends.
deceitful|Trying to make someone believe a lie.|The deceitful fox hid the truth in the story.
deception|Something done to make someone believe what is not true.|The magician's trick was a clever deception.
perceives|Notices or understands something.|The story's owl perceives a shape in the dark.
perceived|Noticed or understood something.|I perceived a quiet sound outside the window.
perceiving|Noticing or understanding something.|The owl was perceiving shapes in the dark.
perception|The way you notice or understand something.|Our perception of the picture changed when we turned it around.
receives|Gets something that is given or sent.|Our school receives letters from children in another country.
received|Got something that was given or sent.|I received a birthday card from my cousin.
receiving|Getting something that is given or sent.|The class is receiving a visit from an author today.
receiver|A person or thing that gets something sent to it.|The receiver of the letter was my cousin.
receivers|People or things that get something sent to them.|The receivers of our cards sent us thank-you notes.
signatures|Names written in people's own special ways.|The authors wrote their signatures inside our books.
temperatures|Measures of how hot or cold things are.|We compared the temperatures of two cups of water.
structure|The way something is built or put together.|The bridge has a strong structure.
structures|Things that have been built or put together.|We built tall structures from wooden blocks.
structural|To do with how something is built and held together.|The bridge needs strong structural supports.
sculpture|A piece of art made by shaping a material.|I made a clay sculpture of a rabbit.
sculptures|Pieces of art made by shaping materials.|Our class displayed the clay sculptures on a shelf.
sculptor|An artist who makes sculptures.|The sculptor shaped a bird from clay.
sculptors|Artists who make sculptures.|The sculptors showed us their stone animals.
texture|How something feels when you touch it.|The bark has a rough texture.
textures|The different ways things feel when you touch them.|We felt the textures of wool, wood and smooth stone.
textured|Having a surface that you can feel.|We used textured paper to make a picture.
pasture|Land covered in grass where farm animals can eat.|The sheep ate grass in the pasture.
pastures|Areas of grass where farm animals can eat.|The cows moved between two green pastures.
departure|The act of leaving a place.|We waved goodbye before the train's departure.
departures|Times when people or vehicles leave a place.|The station board shows the train departures.
moisture|A small amount of water in something or on a surface.|There was moisture on the inside of the window.
treasures|Things that are valuable or very special to someone.|I keep my little treasures in a painted box.
treasured|Loved or valued something very much.|I treasured the picture my friend made for me.
treasuring|Loving or valuing something very much.|She was treasuring the shell her grandad had given her.
pleasures|Things that bring happiness or enjoyment.|Reading stories is one of my favourite pleasures.
feature|An important or noticeable part of something.|The garden's best feature is its huge oak tree.
features|Important or noticeable parts of something.|The drawing shows the bird's main features.
featured|Was included or shown in something.|My picture was featured in the school newsletter.
featuring|Including or showing something.|We read a book featuring a friendly dragon.
fixture|Something fixed in a place so it stays there.|The lamp is a permanent fixture on the wall.
fixtures|Things fixed in place so they stay there.|The classroom's fixtures include its lights and sinks.
gesture|A movement that shows what you mean or how you feel.|A friendly wave is a welcoming gesture.
gestures|Movements that show what you mean or how you feel.|We used hand gestures to tell our story.
measures|Finds out the size or amount of something.|The ruler measures the length of the leaf.
measured|Found out the size or amount of something.|I measured the ribbon with a ruler.
measuring|Finding out the size or amount of something.|We are measuring the height of our sunflower.
measurement|A size or amount that has been measured.|Write the measurement beside your drawing.
measurements|Sizes or amounts that have been measured.|We wrote down the measurements of our tables.
ensure|To make sure something happens or is true.|Please ensure the lid is closed before you shake the pot.

ensured|Made sure something happened or was true.|We ensured that every child had a turn.
ensuring|Making sure something happens or is true.|We are ensuring that everyone has a place in the game.
endure|To keep going through something difficult.|The little plant can endure a cold winter.
endures|Keeps going through something difficult.|The strong tree endures the winter winds.
endured|Kept going through something difficult.|The little plant endured the cold winter.
enduring|Lasting for a long time.|Their enduring friendship began at school.
retrieve|To get something back or bring it back.|The dog ran to retrieve the ball.
retrieves|Gets something back or brings it back.|The dog retrieves the ball from the grass.
retrieved|Got something back or brought it back.|I retrieved my hat from under the bench.
retrieving|Getting something back or bringing it back.|The dog is retrieving its favourite ball.
retrieval|The act of getting something back.|The game involves the retrieval of hidden cards.
